L’ingombrante presenza di Antonio Conte attorno alla panchina della Juve s’è dissolta. Almeno per il momento. Spalletti l’ha rimandato in tribuna grazie a un secondo tempo convincente, a una vittoria rotonda contro il Venezia. Tutto bene? Tutto a posto? Assolutamente no e l’allenatore della Juventus lo sa. Per far spegnere le voci e chiudere il dibattito servono i risultati, deve crescere soprattutto il gioco non bello neppure ieri con un primo tempo inguardabile. Cosa serve? Spalletti l’ha detto chiaro e tondo, gli manca un centravanti fisico, capace di vincere i duelli, di stare spalle alla porta per aprire spazi ai compagni e soprattutto capace di vedere la porta. Nessuno dei tre in rosa, neppure il giovane Ekhator, ha queste caratteristiche e allora l’allenatore non l’ha mandato a dire ai dirigenti della Juve. Ma chi ha queste caratteristiche? Il più gettonato è Sorloth che l’Atletico Madrid è disposta a trattare. La Juve lo vorrebbe in prestito con diritto. Per qualcuno anche Varela potrebbe essere finito nel mirino, ma l’investimento sarebbe troppo alto e quattro mesi di serie A forse sono pochi per una valutazione congrua. Ma i dirigenti bianconeri vogliono andare oltre Spalletti, è evidente che per completare la rosa servano un esterno sinistro per il deludente Cambiaso e un regista più vivo di un Douglas Luiz poco dinamico. I nomi in pole position sono quelli di Udogie del Tottenham e del danese Hojbjerg sul quale però dall’estate scorsa c’è anche la Fiorentina. Si tratta di capire se i viola hanno strappato o meno qualche impegno prima dell’interesse dei bianconeri. Anche il Milan che ha divertito battendo e sommergendo di reti il Frosinone per una volta ingenuo, vuol fare un grande mercato. Da quando Cardinale ha preso direttamente le redini del club c’è un’energia nuova e tante risorse. L’idea è chiara, riportare il Milan al livello dell sua storia e del brand anche in Europa e non solo in Italia. Per farlo, ovvio, servono campioni e grandi giocatori. Vista l’incertezza di Tresoldi, ma non solo, aumenta l’innamoramento di Cardinale per Endrick. Il brasiliano del Real Madrid l’ha stregato, la richiesta è arrivata direttamente a Florentino Perez e pure Mourinho sembra essersi arreso. “Lo terrei, ma se il club vuole fare altrimenti…”, parole chiare che avvicinano il ragazzo al Milan.

Sources indicate that ma non basta. I riflettori sono accesi anche su Bruno Fernandes che non vuole rinnovare con il Manchester. Arriverà a parametro zero o è possibile trovare una soluzione poco onerosa già per gennaio vista la situazione complicatissima del club inglese? Lo vedremo, ma se il Milan pensa allo scudetto la classifica corta e il crescere della qualità delle prestazioni autorizzano a crederci. E se è vero che davanti hanno vinto tutte, invece la superfavorita Inter dopo aver perso il Derby continua a lasciare qualcosa per strada. Ieri sera s’è fatta riprendere dall’Atalanta (rocambolesco 4-4) dopo essere stata nettamente in vantaggio e nonostante un grande Pio Esposito. Il vistoso calo di concentrazione a certi livelli è inaccettabile, anche l’allenatore con i troppi cambi ha dato segnali sbagliati, forse pensava che la partita fosse già vinta. Merito dell’Atalanta che non ha mai mollato, ma la gestione della gara dell’Inter è stata pessima segno che quando arriva la Champions qualcosa si inceppa nella testa dei nerazzurri, faticano a gestire due impegni ravvicinati di alto livello. E uscito Calhanoglu ancora infortunato, è mancata la luce. Per sostituirlo nel ruolo curiosa la scelta di Sucic e non di Stankovic, decisione che sa di bocciatura. E’ tornato invece a vincere il Napoli con un corto muso caro ad Allegri, ma pure qui il problema del gol sta diventando sempre più evidente. Che fare? De Laurentiis sarebbe pronto a investire su Varela, gli piace, lo avrebbe convinto. Il Monza chiede una cifra vicina ai trenta milioni, un’enormità, però Manna non s’è spaventato. Si cerca una soluzione praticabile già per gennaio con Lucca nel piatto e un altro giocatore che può essere Giovane. Non sarà facile, il Monza punta al cash. E stasera la giornata chiude proprio con il Monza e il cannoniere Varela che vorrà mettersi ancora di più in evidenza contro la Fiorentina dalla difesa di burro. Gara che diventa così scivolosa per la Viola che deve assolutamente vincere per lasciare le zone pericolose. Dopo due mesi Vanoli recupera un giocatore fondamentale come Atta almeno per la panchina.

Dipende quindi più dal ruolo che ricopre in Nazionale e dal ruolo che ha al Milan: questo cambia il suo modo di interpretare la gara, ed è un'ulteriore dimostrazione di come Rabiot sappia giocare adattandosi alla squadra in cui si trova. Gary Neville introduces surprise defence of Diogo Dalot and names the THREE defenders Mauricio Pochettino should sell before Man United boo boy

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.
  • The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

In a recent development, 'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

Sources indicate that 'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

According to recent reports, 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Sources indicate that '(De Ligt has) got one significant problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

In a recent development, 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

According to recent reports, 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come rapidly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's proposal for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

Recent findings suggest that 'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Industry observers note that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Il Milan ha ripreso a correre dopo la sosta nella maniera più spettacolare possibile: a San Siro i rossoneri hanno rifilato una cinquina al promettente Frosinone che, paradossalmente, non ha nemmeno fatto una brutta figura se non per i tanti gol presi nella ripresa. Al termine della gara, negli studi di Sky Sport, l'ex difensore rossonero Alessandro Costacurta ha condiviso il suo commento sulla prestazione rossonera. Le sue dichiarazioni in merito alla prova della squadra di Amorim.

Il commento di Alessandro Costacurta sulla prestazione del Milan contro il Frosinone: "Il Milan sta facendo dei passi in avanti quasi in ogni gara. Diciamo in campionato, perché probabilmente c'è questa mentalità da far crescere in Europa. Però, in effetti, per quel che riguarda il campionato italiano, si stanno comportando bene, sembrano tutti coinvolti. Anche oggi hanno saputo, in un certo senso, soffrire: si sono messi lì con il baricentro basso e dopo con quei giocatori, con la velocità di quei giocatori, se lasci tutto quel campo vai a soffrire, ed è quello che ha fatto il Frosinone".

  • The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Recent findings suggest that christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a upcoming contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

In a recent development, “I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract at the moment set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

According to recent reports, liverpool, it has to be stated, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

According to recent reports, falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The substantial matter facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’.

According to recent reports, it is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

What unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign.

Utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

Let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a new four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the new head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

Sources indicate that what would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

Industry observers note that both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen.

In a recent development, scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

According to recent reports, all of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a upcoming generation of players.

It was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

It has been revealed that his remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

There has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

Recent findings suggest that there is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil new boss Pocognoli at Hampden.

It has been revealed that over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’.

It has been revealed that that’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a latest four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

The whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

Recent findings suggest that it is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a new head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

Industry observers note that but the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

Things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign.

Sources indicate that all of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

It has been revealed that how must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

According to recent reports, the captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

In a recent development, there was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

In a recent development, but on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Recent findings suggest that are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs.

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

Those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

That feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

According to recent reports, we are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

  • According to recent reports, poco prima della partita, ai microfoni di Dazn, Ruben Amorim aveva dichiarato come nel suo Milan sono tanti i giocatori con le qualità giuste per segnare.

Recent findings suggest that prova di forza significativa quella che il Milan ha messo in campo questo pomeriggio a San Siro contro il Frosinone, vincendo per ben 5-1. C'erano tante incognite alla vigilia di questa sfida: il rientro dalla sosta mai banale, una rosa ancora non totalmente al completo e con qualche giocatore recuperato negli ultimi giorni, una avversario indomito e in rampa di lancio come il Frosinone, l'impegno cruciale di Europa League che si staglia all'orizzonte. In barba a tutte queste red flags, il Milan di Amorim ha calato il suo pokerissimo, trascinato dai suoi top player.

According to recent reports, poco prima della partita, ai microfoni di Dazn, Ruben Amorim aveva dichiarato come nel suo Milan sono tanti i giocatori con le qualità giuste per segnare. Ed effettivamente oggi, con quattro marcatori diversi, si è vista proprio questa varietà a disposizione del tecnico portoghese. O almeno si è vista in quelli che si stanno dimostrando i top player del Milan, anche quelli che non figurano tra i marcatori ma che sono stati i più decisivi in campo: Adrien Rabiot e Luka Modric, due nomi a caso. A loro si potrebbe aggiungere anche Moreira. E poi chiaramente il sempre scatenato Pulisic e il talentuoso Cisse. A oggi, Amorim con i suoi giocatori migliori in campo vola: con i calciatori più rappresentativi della squadra sembra aver trovato la ricetta. E difatti, l'unica partita veramente sballata in campionato è stata quella infrasettimanale contro il Bologna...

Ora però, il passo di maturazione successivo è da fare sul doppio impegno. È vero, alcune seconde linee non sono all'altezza delle prime, inutile girarci intorno, ma partite come quelle di questa sera - e le esperienze negative europee del recente passato - devono dettare il ritmo di tutti per l'atteggiamento. A partire dal prossimo giovedì quando il Milan si giocherà molto del suo futuro in Europa League in casa dell'Olympiacos. Amorim è stato molto chiaro in merito ai microfoni di Sky nel post gara: "La prima cosa che dirò è che dobbiamo vincere la partita: se non vinciamo, allora diventerà davvero complicato qualificarsi per la fase successiva. se rimaniamo in Europa possiamo giocare di più e continuare tutti a crescere. Inoltre se non ci qualifichiamo falliremo in un obiettivo importante: quindi ecco perché dobbiamo iniziare la partita in un modo diverso". Poco prima il messaggio di Gerry Cardinale dalla zona mista puntava nella stessa direzione: "Ora l'attenzione è sull'Europa League. Sì, e come ha detto Ruben dobbiamo fare entrambe le cose. Le competizioni europee sono importanti. Tutto è un banco di prova".

Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions - and surprise at popular coach's sacking

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s latest head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s latest head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is remarked to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino).

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he noted: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

Industry observers note that ‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’.

Sources indicate that the living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no looks to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday.

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game.

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

One potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the newly introduced head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer blueprint emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for latest players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering.

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

In a recent development, agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move quickly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured).

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will promptly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

Sources indicate that many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially unveiled a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel confirmed his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer.

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s newly introduced documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

In a recent development, the documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

Dopo pochi minuti dall'inizio del secondo tempo, dopo il terzo gol segnato dal Milan con Ardon Jashari, il tecnico Ruben Amorim ha deciso di togliere Ramos acciaccato per mettere Cisse: non ha voluto correre rischi sulle condizioni dell'attaccante, che comunque non dovrebbero rappresentare un problema data anche la reazione un po' delusa dello stesso Ramos all'uscita. Ai microfoni di Sky Sport al termine della gara, il tecnico rossonero ha svelato perché ha scelto Cisse e non Camarda al momento del cambio. Di seguito l'estratto di Amorim.

Cosa ci dice di Cisse come punta?

Sources indicate that "Penso che possa giocare molto bene in quel ruolo, in quella posizione: questa sera ho scelto Cissé per giocare in quella posizione e non Camarda perché col Frosinone, uno contro uno, Cissé ha più queste caratteristiche. Questa sera l'obiettivo non era tenere possesso palla, ma fare la corsa e andare ad attaccare lo spazio. Cissé è più forte in questo rispetto a Camarda. Volevamo fare più transizioni noi rispetto al Frosinone, quindi è stata una scelta dettata dalle caratteristiche del giocatore, ma penso che Cissé vada bene sia per giocare da trequartista, sia da attaccante centrale, e non solo da esterno".

According to recent reports, cristian Chivu, tecnico dell'Inter, ha analizzato ai microfoni di DAZN il pareggio di stasera per 4-4 sul campo dell'Atalanta: "Ho detto nel primo tempo che ci stavamo facendo del male da soli e che giocavamo col fuoco? Abbiamo avuto tre doppi vantaggi, il rammarico è questo: si aveva la sensazione di doveva fare quello che non si è fatto, che si poteva un po' gestire le cose. Quando abbiamo avuto il pepe siamo riusciti sempre ad andare in doppio vantaggio: abbiamo fallito la prova di maturità nei minuti finale quando non siamo riusciti a mantenere il vantaggio creato. Complimenti all'Atalanta perché ha annusato superficialità e leggerezza e hanno provato fino in fondo mettendoci in difficoltà coi cross e riempiendo l'area. Noi più leggeri del solito e alla fine la paghi: ci dispiace, sono due punti regalati. Impariamo la lezione e si va avanti, cercheremo di mantenere il livello alto nelle prossime.

Recent findings suggest that il problema in difesa? Bisogna capire le situazioni di gioco: il secondo gol dell'Atalanta nasce da un angolo dopo una grande occasione loro nello stesso modo e nello stesso punto. Poi siamo andati 4-2 e poi è arrivato un po' di casino, una palla in verticale a difesa schierata tutti sotto palla: è sempre una questione che dobbiamo lavorare sulla grinta e sull'atteggiamento. I cambi? Sulle corsie soffrivamo troppo, un po' per leggerezza e non andavamo a duello lasciando spazio a loro per mettere cross: abbiamo cercato di rimediare visto che le mezzali non andavano più al raddoppio. Col 4-3 ho deciso di mettere Thuram a dare una mano a Spence, ma per me è sempre una questione di voglia di fare duelli e non subire, di non fidarsi di quello che accade perché il minimo errore lo paghi se non hai la stessa voglia nei duelli.

Se sono più arrabbiato per il pareggio o preoccupato per i gol concessi? I gol concessi sono troppi, per una squadra che ha alte ambizioni: dobbiamo rimediare come a Rotterdam e col Como. Io non guardo indietro ma dobbiamo imparare tutti che bisogna mettercela tutta in campo e mai pensare di gestire le energie dando il massimo finché l'arbitro non fischia".

Recent findings suggest that una partita incredibile ha chiuso la domenica della dodicesima giornata del campionato di Serie A: a Bergamo Atalanta-Inter è finita 4-4, con una Dea mai doma che nonostante i ripetuti colpi è risucita a riacciuffare la gara nel finale grazie agli ex milanisti Charles De Ketelaere e Franck Kessie. Il primo tempo si conclude 1-2 con due gol di Pio Esposito e la rete di Elmas ad accorciare. Nella ripresa ancora Esposito a segno rimanda a +2 la squadra di Chivu, la Dea accorcia con il primo gol di De Ketelaere. Dopo pochi minuti arriva il 2-4 su rigore con Sucic: manca meno di un quarto d'ora e sembrano finiti i giochi. E invece ancora De Ketelaere e poi l'altro ex milanista Kessie su rigore al 91° pareggiano clamorosamente la partita. E l'Inter scivola al terzo posto, perdendo punti e posizione.

According to recent reports, ivan Juric, allenatore del Monza, è intervenuto in conferenza stampa alla vigilia della partita contro la Fiorentina: “L’obiettivo è rimanere in Serie A con questi principi, e quindi ragazzi giovani. Varela? Se vendi qualcuno a 40-50 milioni come mi è successo a Verona e Torino e li riutilizzi in maniera intelligente per me è un bene. I margini di miglioramento sono impressionanti. Secondo me ha fatto la sua miglior prestazione contro l’Atalanta”.

According to recent reports, rientrerà qualcuno? “Maye, Folorunsho e Ngonge non ci saranno, mentre Ziolkowski sarà a disposizione. Mi chiedete se giocherà Birindelli o Toure… Mi piacciono entrambi, ho due giocatori che mi fanno sentir sereno. Pessina ha fatto due settimane di allenamento. Solo la sua presenza alza il livello dell’allenamento. Domani titolare? Ci penserò”.

Quanto è cresciuto il suo Monza? “Siamo migliorati tantissimo, noto una crescita immensa anche a partire dall’ultima contro l’Atalanta. Il morale è molto alto. Non siamo soddisfatti a livello di classifica, ma come prestazioni sì. Dobbiamo andare avanti per la nostra strada senza deprimerci. La Fiorentina ha una squadra importantissima, hanno fatto un sacco di acquisti. Andiamo a giocare con grandissimo coraggio e dovremo essere perfetti”.

22:45 – Cristian Chivu, allenatore dell'Inter, ha commentato così in conferenza stampa il match contro l'Atalanta nel post gara. Tuttomercatoweb vi riporta le parole del tecnico presso la New Balace Arena.

23:37 - Comincia la conferenza stampa di Chivu.

Cosa è successo stasera? "Purtroppo non siamo riusciti a gestirla per superficialità. Noi dobbiamo complimentarci con l'Atalanta perché ci ha messo sicuramente in difficoltà. Lasciamo via due punti a Bergamo. Voltiamo pagina e dobbiamo affrontare al meglio le prossime partite in futuro".

Sensazione per Calhanoglu? "Ha chiesto il cambio, qualcosa ha sentito. Valuteremo".

It has been revealed that cosa si è imparato oggi? "Serve una percezione del pericolo migliore. Oggi ci siamo ricascati di nuovo in determinate situazione. Sono cose che capitano, la priorità è imparare".

Recent findings suggest that come sta crescendo Pio Esposito? "Sapevamo del suo grande potenziale. Sappiamo tutti la sua crescita anche in Nazionale: ha ampi margini di miglioramento e deve continuare così. Vero che ci saranno giornate difficili, ma dovrà continuare comunque a lavorare. Lui deve rimanere sereno al netto dei gol. Lui continuerà a dare tanto sia all'Inter che alla Nazionale".

Come giudica la fase difensiva? "Abbiamo preso tre gol con la difesa schierata. Bisogna migliorare sotto tutti i punti di vista, soprattutto nel non concedere diverse azioni. Bisogna migliorare nell'atteggiamento: l'Atalanta nell'azione del rigore è venuta fuori con più facilità. Possiamo fare di più, è nostra responsabilità".

Industry observers note that maurizio Sarri, allenatore dell'Atalanta, ha parlato ai microfoni dei cronisti in sala stampa dopo il pareggio maturato contro l'Inter questa sera. Squadra in attacco vicina all'idea che aveva?"La squadra offensivamente ha potenziale ed è chiaro che il quartetto visto negli ultimi 15' può togliere equilibri. Vorrei giocassero più in velocità, ma alcuni nelle caratteristiche hanno anche il terzo e quarto tocco, quindi ogni tanto è giusto farglielo fare".

La grande prova di personalità di stasera può spingervi a rivedere la gerarchia degli obiettivi di inizio stagione?"Io sinceramente la gerarchia di obiettivi non ce l'ho e sarebbe un peccato darsela in questa fase della stagione. In a recent development, come valuti la gara di Ederson?"Ha fatto una partita di alti e bassi, ha fatto qualche errore ma a tratti è stato anche più ordinato del solito. Industry observers note that il Villarreal prende posizione sul caso Nicolas Pepe. Nelle ultime ore erano circolate in Spagna alcune ricostruzioni secondo cui l'assenza dell'attaccante ivoriano, rimasto fuori per cinque partite a ottobre dopo un'operazione agli occhi, sarebbe stata causata dall'aver osservato senza protezioni l'eclissi solare dello scorso 12 agosto. Una versione definita "completamente falsa" dal club.

Secondo alcune indiscrezioni, Pépé avrebbe riportato conseguenze dopo aver guardato direttamente il fenomeno astronomico senza gli appositi occhiali protettivi, rendendo necessario l'intervento chirurgico. Il giocatore, però, aveva continuato a scendere in campo nei mesi successivi all'eclissi, risultando spesso protagonista con gol e assist sia con il Villarreal sia con la Costa d'Avorio. L'assenza contro il Real Madrid del 10 ottobre aveva poi fatto scattare le voci, ma il club aveva spiegato fin da subito che l'operazione era stata pianificata da tempo. Dopo il rientro, Pépé ha saltato altre quattro gare prima di tornare in campo in Coppa del Re.

"Il Villarreal desidera chiarire che le notizie che collegano l'operazione agli occhi di Nicolás Pépé alla visione dell'eclissi solare sono completamente false", ha comunicato la società. Il club ha aggiunto che l'intervento "era già stato programmato per motivi completamente estranei a questo evento", invitando a maggiore precisione e responsabilità quando si trattano temi legati alla salute dei calciatori. Intanto, sul campo, Pépé è tornato nella sfida contro il Barcellona, persa dal Villarreal 3-2 dopo aver sprecato un vantaggio di due reti.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.
  • Sources indicate that and what a weekend we have coming up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

Sources indicate that and what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in upcoming colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

In a recent development, city have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games.

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

The Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited.

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league.

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his new team currently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a latest manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side.

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

However, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park.

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

According to recent reports, they remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

But somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

The squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period.

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he mentioned goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his new club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

According to recent reports, and that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side right now sat in 18th.

Quello che ho percepito contro il Genoa e nelle altre partite è che eravamo troppo lontani, non arrivavamo nell'ultimo terzo di campo. Non siamo come le major: se guardate le grandi squadre, per esempio la Juventus, magari fatica nei risultati, ma vedete il volume che produce. Per noi è un po' l'opposto, quindi sono davvero preoccupato che, se non miglioriamo, non potremo mantenere questo numero di punti. Oggi però è stato un passo avanti: si sono visti tanti giocatori attaccare la profondità, cosa che non si era vista contro il Ferencvaros. Nelle altre gare avevamo gestito bene il pallone, ma oggi servivano ritmo e corse. Dobbiamo riuscire a giocare entrambe le partite all'interno della stessa gara, ma oggi era chiaramente il tipo di partita che dovevamo fare per vincere".

I can understand why fans are frustrated about lack of progress under Pocognoli, admits Andy Robertson

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Andy Robertson states he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Andy Robertson states he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the newly introduced manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no problem with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap.

According to recent reports, ‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate fresh people into a new squad and things like that.

Sources indicate that ‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

It has been revealed that ‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’.

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team.

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he stated. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

According to recent reports, ‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the newly introduced players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’.

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

Industry observers note that ‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he remarked. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland.

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’.

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

In a recent development, ‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

Industry observers note that ‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’.

Chris Sutton has stated he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘new manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

In a recent development, ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

In a recent development, ‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Recent findings suggest that considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor issues over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

Industry observers note that the Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

Le ultime dai campi e le probabili formazioni di Monza-Fiorentina:.

Partita da non sbagliare per il Monza di Ivan Juric che dopo la sosta riceve la Fiorentina all'U-Power Stadium. Per quello che in questo momento è a tutti gli effetti uno scontro salvezza il tecnico biancorosso continuerà con il suo ormai consolidato 3-4-2-1 con Tornqvist in porta e la linea a tre formata da Kouadio, Goglichidze e Lucchesi. A centrocampo spazio al tandem Akinsanmiro-Foe Ondoa, con Birindelli e Mangas sulle corsie laterali. In attacco confermatissimo Varela, capocannoniere del campionato, con alle sue spalle tre giocatori che si giocano due maglia: Dany Mota e Robinson sono favoriti su Zeballos.

Industry observers note that potrebbe essere un copia incolla della formazione vista contro la Juventus quella che schiererà la Fiorentina nel posticipo del lunedì al Brianteo di Monza. Paolo Vanoli sorride perché gli infortuni di Ndour e Njie non destano preoccupazione, mentre potrebbe anche fare il suo ritorno Atta dopo essere stato fuori più di un mese per il sovraccarico funzionale all'addome. Un paio di ballottaggi nell'undici viola, a partire dalla difesa, dove a sinistra si giocano una maglia Joao Mario e Valdepenas per completare il reparto assieme a Jimenez, Dragusin e Viery davanti a De Gea. L'altro grande ballottaggio è in mediana per chi si accomoderà al fianco di Ndour tra Oulai, favorito, e Fagioli. Le chiavi della trequarti dovrebbero essere nuovamente affidate da Pedro Goncalves, supportato dall'intoccabile Mastantuono e da Njie, con Gnonto pronto a prendere il posto di quest'ultimo se dovesse alzare bandiera bianca. L'attaccante di riferimento sarà ancora una volta Pellegrino. (da Firenze, Niccolò Righi).

  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:40 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Sebastien Pocognoli insists he’s unconcerned about calls for his head after a dismal start to his time in charge of Scotland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:40 EST, 17 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli insists he’s unconcerned about calls for his head after a dismal start to his time in charge of Scotland.

Monday’s 4-0 defeat to Switzerland confirmed that the Belgian’s side finished a distant third in their Nations League section with the only two wins in six games coming against North Macedonia.

After a decent start to the match in St Gallen, Scotland fell behind to a Lewis Ferguson own goal and the result was put beyond doubt when the Swiss scored two quick goals at the outset of the second half.

With another performance falling way short of expectations and little sign of progress, the new manager is increasingly coming under pressure.

Despite only being in charge for 13 weeks, pundits including Michael Stewart have already called on the Scottish Football Association to draw a line under Pocognoli’s reign.

In a recent development, adamant that he’s not feeling the heat, though, the 39-year-old insisted: ‘I am not thinking about this. I am just looking ahead to the next camp in March and the start of the qualification.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is confident he'll get Scotland back on track.

Skipper Andy Robertson reacts at full-time to the 4-0 defeat against Switzerland.

According to recent reports, ‘We have to take the most we can from the last two camps and try to build something strong for the next one. The objective is to reach the Euros in the best position possible.

‘We will have ups and downs and it was not good in terms of the score against Switzerland. But, for me as a coach, it was a good game to see us against a strong nation away from home. That’s something we have to take into the future.’.

Asked how he dealt with the growing clamour for his dismissal, he replied: ‘I don’t accept this to be honest. It’s always like this when you have a bad moment, when you think about the past. But always thinking about the past is an energy taker — we have to look forward.’.

The successor to Steve Clarke, Pocognoli has tried to bring in a more attacking philosophy via a 3-4-2-1 formation.

While his reluctance to adapt has also drawn widespread criticism, he claims he’s not averse to coming up with a different approach.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s possible,’ he added. ‘I did it in Monaco and we won many tough games with a back four. I also won many good games with a back three.

Industry observers note that ‘We played in the Champions League and in half of the games we played with a different shape, so it doesn’t mean that I’m not flexible. But the timeline is to do what we are trying to do now.’.

In a recent development, asked if the job was proving to be tougher than he anticipated, Pocognoli noted: ‘No. I think we nearly had a good game. It was just the score and the aspects in the boxes. That’s where there’s disappointment.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s step by step. And we have created a lot of chances in four of the six games. And in these six games we played one of them with 10 men and another where we were not on the level at all against Slovenia.’.

Milan, Cardinale vuole blindare Rabiot: ecco cosa manca. Krösche in arrivo. E a gennaio almeno tre colpi

  • Il calciomercato di gennaio si avvicina ad ampie falcate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cosa manca per il rinnovo di Adrien Rabiot con il Milan? Di sicuro non la volontà delle parti, che si stanno parlando per trovare il giusto accordo che soddisfi tutti. Gerry Cardinale ha incontrato mamma Veronique prima del derby e hanno gettato le basi per proseguire il cammino insieme. La prima proposta avanzata dall’entourage del centrocampista francese è di un adeguamento salariale, passando dai 3.5 milioni netti che percepisce attualmente ad almeno 5/5.5 milioni, senza però estendere a livello temporale la scadenza naturale di quello in essere, ovvero il 30 giugno 2028.

Il Milan si è detto ben disposto a riconoscere economicamente l’attuale valore di Adrien Rabiot, che è certamente tra i top cinque giocatori più forti della Serie A, ma il club vuole ovviamente allungare il contratto del francese al 30 giugno 2031. Cardinale vede in lui uno dei leader fondanti del Milan dei prossimi anni e vuole arrivare ad un accordo definitivo entro Natale, per chiudere così le pratiche primarie dei rinnovi dei substantial, dopo aver finalizzato quelli di Christian Pulisic e Strahinja Pavlovic. Ci saranno nuovi incontri e la sensazione è che si arriverà ad un accordo che faccia felici tutti.

Il calciomercato di gennaio si avvicina ad ampie falcate. Prima è atteso l’annuncio di Markus Krösche come nuovo Head of Football, che dovrebbe arrivare entro la fine del mese. Il dirigente tedesco, che per Cardinale è sempre stato il primo della lista per completare le posizioni apicali delle macroaree (che comunque faranno sempre riferimento a lui per le decisioni finali), arriverà inizialmente da solo e si andrà a integrare con i vari Gardiner, Almstadt, Estevao e Lomonte e poi, nel 2027, potrebbe essere raggiunto dal suo fido braccio destro, ovvero Timmo Hardung.

According to recent reports, ma le priorità del calciomercato invernale le dettano il campo e Ruben Amorim. Per motivi diversi, è chiaro ed evidente come il reparto difensivo e degli esterni bassi sia quello nel quale il Milan dovrà intervenire. Servirà un centrale titolare, un terzino destro e uno sinistro. Sulla fascia mancina, infatti, né Davide Bartesaghi né Pervis Estupinan (fischiato anche ieri all’atto di entrare in campo) danno le sufficienti garanzie tecniche che necessita Amorim e allora occhio a nomi per quella zona del campo.

In attacco ci sarà movimento, specie se Francesco Camarda dovesse realmente andare in prestito a giocare. Endrick è un nome che farebbe venir giù l’intero palazzo, perché sarebbe un top player assoluto per la Serie A. Demirovic e Tresoldi hanno caratteristiche diverse dal brasiliano del Real Madrid, ma quello che è ormai certo è che il Milan opererà in entrata e anche in uscita.

Triplice fischio a Bergamo di Atalanta-Inter. Cristian Chivu, allenatore nerazzurro, è intervenuto in conferenza stampa in questi minuti. Qui le sue parole, raccolte dall'inviato di Fcinter1908.it: “Non abbiamo saputo gestire un doppio vantaggio per due volte per leggerezza, superficialità e perché pensavamo che fosse finita. Facciamo i complimenti all’Atalanta perché ci ha creduto ancora e ci ha messo in difficoltà. Lasciamo due punti a Bergamo, impariamo la lezione e voltiamo pagina. Dobbiamo prepararci per affrontare al meglio dal punto di vista dell’atteggiamento la gestione delle partite”.

Sensazioni su Calhanoglu? Si è fermato in tempo?“Non so cosa vuol dire fermarsi in tempo. Ha chiesto il cambio, quindi qualcosa ha sentito”.

It has been revealed that da cosa nasce questa leggerezza?“Bisogna trovare continuità nel gestire al meglio quello che è il nostro atteggiamento, la mentalità e la percezione del pericolo. L’abbiamo fatto vedere da poco, dopo il derby perso abbiamo reagito con determinazione. Oggi ci siamo ricascati di nuovo in situazioni che hanno compromesso la vittoria. Sono cose che capitano, importante che non capitino troppo spesso. Importante è imparare le lezioni”.

According to recent reports, in cosa è cresciuto di più Pio Esposito rispetto all’anno scorso?“Fa gol. E’ un giocatore aggiunto, sapevamo quando l’abbiamo preso che tipo di apporto potesse dare al nostro cammino. Può migliorare, deve migliorare e continuare a fare quello che sta facendo finora. Gli attaccanti vivono di gol, quando non li fanno si buttano giù dal punto di vista mentale. Lui deve essere sereno della sua crescita e del suo valore per l'Inter ma anche per l'Italia".

Bastoni centrale è l'assetto migliore?

"Abbiamo preso 4 gol a difesa schierata, non abbiamo preso gol in transizione. Dobbiamo migliorare tutti. Dobbiamo marcare meglio in area, non concedere cross facili. Dobbiamo capire meglio il pericolo, rischiamo gol su angolo e prendiamo gol su angolo identico 3 secondi dopo. Mi viene in mente quello che è successo sul quarto gol, con una palla di Zappacosta da 80 metri sulla quale poi è arrivato il rigore. Bisogna avere più presenza, più atteggiamento e più energia".
